name: California State University San Marcos
overview:
California State University San Marcos (CSUSM) is part of the 23 California State University network.

San Marcos has quickly become the main educational center in northern San Diego County with modern buildings, advanced computer technology and state-of-the-art scientific laboratories.

San Marcos is located in the north of the San Diego region (in the heart of the southern California coastal region), 50 kilometers north of the city of San Diego and 150 kilometers south of Los Angeles. Just minutes from campus are the most beautiful deserts, the most beautiful mountains and the most beautiful beaches in California where you can swim, surf, hike, bike and ski. You can also easily reach the San Diego Zoo, Sea World, Disneyland and Hollywood.
administrative:
1. Application dossier

You will work directly with the partner university regarding your application. All required documents will have to be uploaded on their platform or sent by email before the deadline (see the Americas Teams channel for each application deadline). If you have not received anything yet, it means your nomination has not been sent yet, please be patient.


In the past the partner has asked for the following:

  • Photocopy of passport / Residence permit (valid more than 6 months after return)
  • A letter from the bank (less than 3 months old) stipulating the amount of $16,500 or more for the full year format and for the deferred start. Unlike in previous years, the university now only accepts a bank letter for the entire stay. If the bank letter is made from a parent's bank account, an additional letter, written by the parent in question in English, must be provided attesting to the relationship and mentioning that the amount available may be used for your expenses for your academic stay in the United States.
  • Registration form.
  • The partner university will contact you directly for the choice of courses.
  • Certificate in English with your Tepitech score


This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


To be given to Epitech bachelor campus administration to reenroll for the Tech4 (in April/May):

  • The addendum to the contract.
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier.


2.Visa (more information here)

You can find all the detailed information on the US government website or the Embassy of the US in Paris website.


1. Admission letter and I-20 form

When you have been admitted to the university, you will receive an acceptance letter and an I-20 form, allowing you to apply for the F-1 student visa at the embassy. Please check the information on I-20 carefully and sign the document.


2.Pay the SEVIS fees

 You must then pay the SEVIS I-901 fees online (here). Make sure you print the receipts. The fees for students are $350.


3.Complete the DS-160 form

Complete DS-160 form and upload an ID photo meeting the following requirements. Print the application form confirmation page to bring to your interview.

You will have to pay a visa application fee (non refundable) before your interview of $185 (more information here).


4.Schedule an appointment at the consulate

For people in France, you need to make an appointment for your interview at the US Consulate. Plan to travel to Paris for it.

If you live in another country, check the different consulate/embassy.

You can check the deadlines for obtaining an appointment for submitting a file, here.


During your interview at the consulate, you must:

  • have the necessary supporting documents to prove that you qualify for the category of visa that you request--document relating to your current studies and its relationship to the studies you wish to pursue in the United States: academic transcript, various certificates, SAT or TOEFL test scores, diplomas, etc.
  • demonstrate, with supporting evidence, to the consular officer that you have solid family, social and financial ties to France and that you intend to return there once your residence permit has expired.
  • prove that you have the financial means necessary to finance your studies and live in good conditions in the United States for the first 12 months. Any document proving your family or relational ties with any person funding your studies, as well as bank statements, tax notices thereof.

Please note that the visa gives you the right to work 20 hours on campus.


3.Insurance and Health

Option 1: Subscribe to CSUSM insurance (more information here and here)

To meet the health insurance requirement, we suggest you purchase the CSU-sponsored health insurance which meets the Health Insurance Requirements.

Annual costs: $1788 (2026). Costs for 5 months: $745.


Option 2: Choose a private international insurance (more information here)

You must submit a petition to the Office of Global Education to approve your alternative policy. The petition must be accompanied by documentation clearly describing (in English) the policy benefits and restrictions.


Please note that alternate insurance plans must meet these requirements:

  • The medical benefit is unlimited, with a deductible of no more than $150.
  • The policy is valid as long as you are enrolled at CSUSM.
  • The repatriation benefit is at least $7,500.
  • The medical evacuation benefit is at least $10,000.
  • The policy provides equal benefits for men and women.
  • The policy includes prenatal (pregnancy) and maternity coverage at no extra cost.
  • The policy pays for pre-existing conditions after six months of continuous coverage. 


It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.


Additionally, CSUSM requires proof of vaccinations prior to course registration. Your vaccines must therefore be up to date before returning to school.

  • Tuberculosis (TB): You must provide a negative tuberculosis test, done within 6 months of entering the USA.
  • Measles, rubella and mumps (MMR): You must be vaccinated against measles, rubella and mumps before your arrival.
  • Hepatitis B (for those under 18): If you are under 18 during the orientation session, you must provide proof of your hepatitis B vaccination.


"Immunization form" which confirms the vaccination of students is to be provided to San Marcos once there but you must send it to us before on the intra for verification.

For more information, you can consult the country’s health file at: https://www.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fr/conseils-aux-voyageurs/conseils-par-pays-destination/etats-unis/


Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.


4.Prepare your arrival

For advice to travelers issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on the country, click here.

Check out the university’s page for international students here.

Check the International Student Checklist provided by the university here.


Make your travel plans early. San Marcos is about 60 km north of the San Diego International Airport (SAN) and 160 km south of the Los Angeles International Airport (LAX). We strongly recommend that you arrive at the San Diego International Airport. If you have to change planes in the U.S., you must allow at least three hours to go through immigration and find your connecting flight. 


You must make your own travel arrangements from the airport to San Marcos.  We recommend that you arrive at the San Diego International Airport. If you arrive in San Diego, and you are living in homestay, then you may reserve airport transportation with the homestay company. You may also reserve an airport shuttle from Los Angeles International Airport, but this can cost about $200 and can take 2 hours to get to San Marcos. Flights from Los Angeles to San Diego cost between $50 - $150. You must reserve a shuttle or arrange your transportation before you leave your home country.  CSUSM does not provide airport transportation.


Shuttles at the airport include Supershuttle, Seabreezeshuttle, or Vango.


5.Campus life

The 120 hectare campus is located in San Marcos, a small, quiet community with many restaurants and shops.

The number of students per class is limited, which allows individualized instruction, and the classrooms and laboratories are new and equipped with the latest technology.


There are apartment-style university residences on campus, where life is buzzing with more than 80 clubs and organizations, art conferences, movies, concerts, and guest speakers.

Off-campus accommodation (more information here)

The San Marcos, Carlsbad, Escondido, Oceanside, and Vista communities near CSU San Marcos offer many reasonably priced apartments. The following sites may be useful in your search for off-campus housing, apartments and room rentals.

A 2 bedroom apartment is around $2,100 / month. It is cheaper to find a house / apartment for 3 or more (a 3-person apartment in a residence is about 2400$, or ~800$ per person compared to + 1000$ for two)


  • Studio or room in a shared apartment

You can find announcements on these websites: Apartmentguide, Cirtru, Apartments.

You can also check out this Facebook group created by students for listing items for sale, housing and roommates. CSUSM does not monitor or endorse the listings.


  • Host family

Price : $800- $900/month (may be subject to fluctuations). Breakfasts and dinners are included from Monday to Friday. Well located in San Marcos and the surrounding cities. Please note : registration fees and a deposit may be required.


- How are they selected?

Students submit an application with choices & personal details (e.g. willingness to live with young children/pets, any allergies, etc.) and then the host provider will provide them with options that the students can then rank. This is the ideal circumstance that students get choice. That said, when availability starts to decrease, it is possible that the homestay provider may place based on the preferences written in the application.


- Are they generally close to campus or would students need a car?

The general guideline is that students should be able to get from their host family to CSUSM campus in 45 minutes or less. This could mean walking, biking, or public transportation. So, a car is not necessary. That said, if a student plans to buy a car, they should mention this in their application as it could provide more host family options.

You may contact the following homestay agencies directly to apply for homestay (CSUSM does not monitor or endorse these agencies).


  • 4 Stay
  • FA Homestay

Credits

Number of local credits to be earned per year: 24

Number of local credits to be earned per semester: 12


Academic Calendar

  • Fall semester: mid-August to mid-December
  • Spring semester: mid-January to mid-May


Department and Courses (more information here)

Teaching is provided in English at the American Language and Culture Institute - Computer Science Department.


For the Fall semester (1st semester), you must follow the following rule concerning the classes:

  • 2 IT classes (starting with CS)
  • 1 non-IT class
  • 2 English classes
  • Totalling 15 local credits (= units)

Course Format and Workload

CSU San Marcos teaching is more theoretical than Epitech: expect homework, lecture-style classes, required presence.


Important Notes

  • Presence in class is compulsory, under penalty of loss of visa and repatriation to France at the student's expense (impact on credits).
  • The courses are most likely more academic than at EPITECH.
  • The course list is given for information only. It can change from year to year.
  • If a course is not available when you arrive on site, EPITECH cannot be held responsible for it.,
  • Any Tech 4 abroad involves an EIP! Take advantage of the free slots you will have to advance it.
cost:
Financial Overview (4th Year EPITECH)

  • You must pay the tuition fees for the 4th year of EPITECH, as well as the re-registration fees and related fees.
  • EPITECH covers the application fees and part of the tuition fees. Epitech covers tuition only for required credits.
  • The tuition supplement payable by you is indicated at the top of this page (if applicable).
  • Other costs at your expense include: travel, accommodation on site, insurance, and everyday expenses (books, food, transport, etc.).


Other Expenses

  • Round trip: around 1,000€
  • Insurance: 300-600€ depending on the coverage or $573.00 for Spring 2017 and $358.00 for Summer 2017 if you choose the insurance through university
  • Visa: about 500€


Estimated Budget

The local currency is the Dollar. 1 € = 1.16USD (rate as of October 2025).

Please check the Numbeo website to compare the cost of living between your city of origin and your city of exchange. Please note that everyone's budget will be different according to one's lifestyle.

For the living costs, you must plan to have $16,500 for your year abroad.


Housing: see prices here for on-campus housing
